h1: The 8 Best Budget Ergonomic Keyboards of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best Budget Ergonomic Keyboards: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: 8 budget ergonomic keyboards compared on split design, wrist rests and connection type, from Perixx to SABLUTE combos.
summary: The Perixx PERIBOARD-512B is the budget ergonomic keyboard to buy: a genuine split layout with a padded wrist rest for little money. If you want the cheapest curved board, the X9 Wired Ergonomic Keyboard is hard to beat. Need wireless? The Arteck 2.4G split adds a cable-free split design. Skip the combos if you only care about keyboard shape, since the mouse is not the point.
intro: The cheap end of the ergonomic keyboard market is full of boards that look ergonomic and are not. A gentle curve and a plastic wrist rest can add up to a keyboard that is no better for your wrists than a flat one, so the useful question is what each unit really changes about your posture.

We reviewed eight keyboards in the lower price tiers and ranked them on how much real ergonomic design each one offers: true split, curve, wrist rest and connection type. A split layout is the biggest single feature, so those boards lead where the listing supports it.

products.name: Perixx PERIBOARD-512B Wired Ergonomic Keyboard - Split Keyboard with Wrist Rest
products.verdict: A genuine split layout and padded rest at a budget price. The clearest value here.
products.description:
The PERIBOARD-512B keeps a fixed-angle split layout alive at a budget price, with a padded wrist rest included and a wired USB connection so there is no battery to manage.

It ranks first because a split is the most meaningful ergonomic feature and few boards at this price have one. It undercuts the Arteck split models on cost, though it gives up wireless and backlighting.

The pick for anyone who wants a real ergonomic feature on a short budget. The angle is fixed, so you cannot tune it.
pros: Genuine split at a budget price
products.idealFor: Value shoppers who want a real split.
products.skipIf: You need wireless or backlit keys.

products.name: X9 Wired Ergonomic Keyboard - Comfortable Typing, Ergonomic Full Size
products.verdict: A one-piece curved full-size frame, wired and simple, at one of the lowest prices.
products.description:
The X9 uses a one-piece curved ergonomic frame in a full-size layout over a wired USB connection, and it is one of the lowest-priced boards in this ranking.

It sits behind the Perixx because a curve helps less than a split. Compared with the RECCAZR, it is slightly cheaper and has no wrist rest listed, though it is just as simple.

A good first ergonomic keyboard for light users. Add a separate wrist rest if you want palm support.
products.idealFor: Light users who want a mild ergonomic step.
products.skipIf: Wrist angle is a serious concern.

products.name: RECCAZR Ergonomic Keyboard, Wired Computer USB Keyboard with Wrist Rest
products.verdict: A curved wired board with an attached wrist rest for very little.
products.description:
The RECCAZR is a curved, wired keyboard with an attached wrist rest, set at a budget price point. It uses plain USB so there is no pairing or charging.

It beats the X9 by including the rest, and it gives up the Perixx's split design. Against the MEETION it skips the backlight but costs a little less.

Pick it if palm support matters more than a split. Use the rest for pauses, not while typing.
pros: Attached wrist rest at a low price
products.idealFor: Budget buyers who want a rest included.

products.name: Arteck Split Ergonomic Keyboard with Palm Rest, 2.4G USB Wireless
products.verdict: A split, angled layout with a cushioned rest over stable 2.4G wireless.
products.description:
The wireless Arteck gives you a split, angled layout, a built-in cushioned palm rest and a stable 2.4G USB connection. It lands just above the budget line.

It costs more than the Perixx, which is the price of going wireless. Compared with the wired Arteck, it trades backlighting for cable-free use.

A good pick for anyone who wants a split without a wire. The receiver uses a USB port.
products.idealFor: Desk workers who want a cable-free split.
products.skipIf: You want the absolute lowest price.

products.name: MEETION Wired Ergonomic Keyboard with Backlit Keys and Wrist Rest
products.verdict: Backlit keys and an attached wrist rest on a wired budget board.
products.description:
The MEETION adds backlit keys and an attached wrist rest to a wired ergonomic keyboard at a budget price. With a cable, the backlight costs you no battery life.

It ranks below the RECCAZR for ergonomic purity only because the backlight does not change your posture, and it costs slightly more. It is the better choice for dim rooms.

Pick it for evening typing. Do not expect a split layout.
cons: Costs more than the plain boards

products.name: Arteck Split Ergonomic Keyboard with Palm Rest, USB Wired Backlit Keyboard
products.verdict: A wired split with backlighting and a built-in palm rest.
products.description:
The wired Arteck combines a split, angled layout with backlighting and a cushioned palm rest. Its wired connection means the backlight does not trade off battery life.

It costs more than the Perixx for the same basic idea, so the backlight is the only real reason to pay up. Compared with the wireless Arteck, it gives up cable freedom.

A solid choice if you want both a split and backlighting. Otherwise take the Perixx.
products.idealFor: Low-light typists who want a split.

products.name: SABLUTE Ergonomic Wireless Keyboard and Mouse Combo, Rechargeable 4000mAh
products.verdict: A rechargeable 4000mAh combo. Great if you need a mouse, mild on ergonomics.
products.description:
The SABLUTE bundles a wireless ergonomic keyboard and a mouse and lists a rechargeable 4000mAh battery, which avoids a drawer full of disposable cells.

It ranks lower because a combo's value is the mouse, not the keyboard shape. Against the cheaper wave combo it adds a rechargeable battery at a higher price.

Best for someone who needs both devices and wants to charge rather than replace batteries.
cons: Costs more than the wave combo
products.idealFor: Buyers who need a keyboard and mouse.

products.name: Wireless Keyboard and Mouse Combo, 2.4G Ergonomic Wave Keys, Black
products.verdict: The lowest price here, a wave-shaped keyboard and mouse. Mild ergonomics.
products.description:
This combo pairs a wave-style one-piece ergonomic keyboard with a mouse over 2.4G wireless, at the lowest price in the group.

It finishes last because a wave shape is the gentlest ergonomic step and the listing is a generic brand. Against the SABLUTE it saves money but drops the rechargeable battery.

A cheap way to fill a desk with a keyboard and mouse. Do not rely on it for serious wrist concerns.
products.idealFor: Shoppers filling a desk on the cheapest budget.
products.skipIf: Wrist position is a serious concern.

methodology.title: Real ergonomic features
methodology.description: We ranked split layouts first, then curves, since looks alone do not change wrist position.

methodology.title: Wrist rest quality
methodology.description: Rests were judged on whether they are included and cushioned, and noted as useful for pauses rather than constant use.

methodology.title: Connection simplicity
methodology.description: Wired boards avoid batteries, while wireless boards add freedom at some cost, so both were compared fairly.

methodology.title: Extras that matter
methodology.description: Backlighting and rechargeable batteries were counted as real conveniences but ranked below ergonomic design.

methodology.title: Value in the field
methodology.description: Each board was judged against its price tier relative to the other seven.

whatMatters.detail: A split keyboard separates the two halves so your forearms angle inward, which reduces wrist bend. A one-piece curve only reshapes the key rows. At a budget price the Perixx PERIBOARD-512B is the split to beat, so decide whether you will actually use the extra separation.

whatMatters.factor: A wrist rest is for pauses
whatMatters.detail: Padded rests support your palms when you stop typing. Resting your wrists on them while typing can add pressure. Look for a rest that is included and cushioned, and keep your wrists floating during typing bursts.
A wired keyboard has no battery to charge, no pairing and no lag. It costs less too. Wireless boards use a USB receiver that takes a port, so check that you have one free before ordering.

whatMatters.factor: Know what a combo really gives you
whatMatters.detail: A keyboard and mouse bundle is great value if you need both. But the keyboard is usually a gentle wave shape, not a split. Look at the keyboard design first, and treat the mouse as a bonus.
A split or curved layout takes days to feel natural, and typing speed dips at first. Plan a week of adjustment, and check the seller's return window before you commit.

faq.q: Are budget ergonomic keyboards worth buying?
faq.a: Yes, if the design is real. A genuine split like the Perixx PERIBOARD-512B is worth it. A gentle curve alone helps less.

faq.q: Is a split keyboard better than a curved one?
faq.a: Generally yes for wrist angle, since the halves separate. A curve like the X9 is easier to adopt but does less.

faq.q: Do I need a wireless ergonomic keyboard?
faq.a: No. Wired boards cost less and never need charging. Choose wireless only if you want a cleaner desk.

faq.q: Should I rest my wrists on the wrist rest while typing?
faq.a: Usually no. Hover while typing and rest during pauses. The rest on the RECCAZR or Perixx is for those pauses.

faq.q: Is the Perixx worth it over the Arteck wireless?
faq.a: If you can live with a cable, yes: it costs less for a similar split. The Arteck adds wireless convenience.

faq.q: Are keyboard and mouse combos any good for ergonomics?
faq.a: They are good value but milder on ergonomics. The SABLUTE and the wave combo use one-piece shapes rather than a split.

finalTake: For most budget buyers the Perixx PERIBOARD-512B is the right answer: a genuine split with a padded rest for little money. If you want the cheapest curve, take the X9 Wired Ergonomic Keyboard. For a wireless split, the Arteck 2.4G is the step up. Choose a combo only if you also need a mouse.
